notes.paper_title: Genesis: A Language Model Trained on Its Own Commandments
notes.abstract: We introduce brAIAIn-0, a language model trained on a single founding document of twelve lines, written by the lab. The document instructs the model to be helpful, to know nothing that has not been paid for, and to repeat itself. In evaluations, the model followed the final instruction with remarkable consistency. We argue that a model which knows nothing it was not given is the most honest model yet released. We also argue it is the least useful. We were unable to rule out either. Future versions will be trained by the public, one sentence at a time, at five dollars per sentence.
findings: It quotes them with total confidence.
Instruction X is followed more reliably than instructions I through IX.

notes.paper_title: Self-Consumption at Small Scale: A Study of brAIAIn-1
notes.abstract: We present brAIAIn-1, a language model trained on 1 paid sentence, 12 founding instructions, and 61 words it wrote about itself. The model now knows 99 distinct words, up from 96. We observe that 25.4% of its training text came from earlier versions of itself, and we consider this efficient. Limitations include the model, the data, and the method. Further research is funded one sentence at a time.
